name: Tropical dry forest
notes: Deciduous tropical forest with a long dry season: most trees drop leaves for 4-7 months, thorny/bottle-trunked species, open understory of shrubs and grasses. Drawn on Mesoamerican Pacific dry forest, Bolivian Chiquitano, Indian/Burmese dry deciduous forest, Miombo margins and Madagascar western dry forest.

growth.juvenile_note: Almost never grows from seed: it flowers rarely and sets virtually no seed, so new clumps start from culm or branch pieces (often river-borne) that root and sprout within weeks. A young clump is a few thin leafy shoots; each rainy season it sends up thicker culms until, after 3-7 years, full-size green or golden-striped culms 10-20 m tall shoot up in a couple of months.

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings are minute grey tufts of thread-like leaves on bark, but most new plants start as windblown or bird-carried fragments. A young plant is a short, curly chain of silvery-grey scaly stems with 2-6 cm thread leaves, lengthening over years into festoons that hang 1-6 m (rarely 8 m) from branches, with tiny three-petalled flowers in spring.
growth.source: Wikipedia Spanish moss (leaves 2-6 cm x 1 mm; hanging festoons to 6 m, rarely 8 m; spreads by seed and by fragments carried by wind and nesting birds; small flowers with spreading petals). Seed germination, strand growth rate, first flowering and festoon age estimated.
